topic: Allocation-regret and LIL-width frontier for anytime whole-curve QTE inference, with the presolve capsule embedded in this queued entry.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp Pareto frontier, over predictable two-arm allocation rules, between whole-curve Neyman allocation regret and the maximal LIL-normalized width of an anytime-valid QTE band on a fixed quantile interval.

source_refs.claim: Derives a quantile-specific design-based efficiency bound and response-adaptive allocations attaining it at a fixed horizon.
source_refs.author: Zhonghua Li, Lan Luo, Jingshen Wang, and Long Feng

source_refs.claim: Obtains anytime logarithmic Neyman regret for ATE estimation relative to the hindsight-optimal fixed design, but not for a quantile-indexed causal curve.
source_refs.author: Georgy Noarov, Riccardo Fogliato, Martin Andres Bertran, and Aaron Roth

source_refs.claim: Gives simultaneous time-and-quantile confidence sequences with the optimal square-root log-log time rate for an i.i.d. quantile process.
source_refs.author: Steven R. Howard and Aaditya Ramdas

source_refs.claim: Introduces Neyman regret for design-based ATE estimation and proves a square-root-time regret bound for Clip-OGD.
source_refs.author: Jessica Dai, Paula Gradu, and Christopher Harshaw

source_refs.excerpt: V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta(q)}=\Theta(q^{1-2\beta}) uniformly over that class of spacing functions.
They make no assertion of a uniform local-oracle ratio involving \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\)

open_problems.why_unsolved: ATE Neyman-regret analyses optimize one scalar inverse-probability variance, while QTE-efficient allocation varies with the quantile index through arm-specific densities and distributional features, forcing one experiment to serve a continuum of incompatible oracle allocations. The prior rollout construction reduces design choice to the largest eigenvalue of a finite covariance matrix, but whole-curve QTE width depends on an infinite-dimensional covariance kernel and two local quantile-spacing functions learned on the same path. Plug-in allocation changes realized quadratic variation and the stopping boundary, so the finite Rayleigh-quotient argument must be replaced by a functional loss characterization and a lower bound separating unavoidable exploration from avoidable allocation loss.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax lower bound characterizing achievable curve-wise allocation-regret and supremum LIL-width pairs, together with an explicit oracle allocation functional and a predictable design-confidence-sequence construction attaining the frontier uniformly over time and quantile index.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest econometric motivation and design formulation for allocating observations specifically to learn a QTE.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mean effects hide distributional heterogeneity -> QTE is the relevant causal curve -> response-adaptive assignment can improve QTE precision -> one allocation must balance whole-curve precision, anytime validity, and allocation regret

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the clipped online-gradient design and pathwise regret decomposition, replacing scalar ATE variance loss by a supremum or dual-mixture loss indexed by quantiles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves anytime regret against a hindsight-optimal design, which is the comparison required by the allocation side of the frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over stitched empirical-process supermartingales and CDF-to-quantile inversion yielding finite-LIL boundaries simultaneously over time and quantiles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the sharp whole-quantile-curve LIL benchmark, but without adaptive treatment propensities.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the QTE efficient influence-function variance and optimal-propensity calculation as the quantile-indexed loss whose online regret must be controlled.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies each quantile's oracle allocation target, from which the functional benchmark can be constructed.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a covariate-adjusted AIPW estimator of the entire QTE curve under predictable response-adaptive assignment whose confidence band is uniform in time and quantile and attains the local semiparametric LIL constant.

source_refs.claim: Constructs efficient fixed-time inference and confidence sequences for scalar ATEs under adaptive assignment and leaves other causal estimands open.
source_refs.author: Thomas Cook, Alan Mishler, and Aaditya Ramdas

source_refs.claim: Provides time- and value-uniform CDF bands for nonstationary data, including importance-weighted counterfactual reward distributions.
source_refs.author: Paul Mineiro and Steven R. Howard

source_refs.claim: Establishes weak convergence uniformly in quantile index and bootstrap QTE bands under covariate-adaptive randomization at a fixed horizon.
source_refs.author: Yichong Zhang and Xin Zheng

source_refs.claim: Attains a semiparametric QTE variance bound with response-adaptive designs, but its theory is fixed-horizon rather than time-uniform and whole-curve.
source_refs.author: Zhonghua Li, Lan Luo, Jingshen Wang, and Long Feng

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing ingredients solve different margins: adaptive AIPW confidence sequences concern a scalar mean, adaptive counterfactual CDF bands are importance-weighted rather than locally semiparametrically efficient, and econometric QTE-process results are fixed-horizon or use assignment dependence not driven by accrued outcomes. Extending the AIPW score to an outcome-threshold-indexed martingale requires predictable nuisance learning, uniform score-class control, and nonlinear quantile inversion; achieving the local density-scaled LIL constant also rules out a loose threshold union bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit sequential AIPW QTE-process estimator and confidence band with time-and-quantile-uniform coverage and a width expansion whose leading constant equals the efficient influence-process standard deviation divided by the relevant potential-outcome densities.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing directly links adaptive assignment, semiparametric efficiency, optional stopping, and confidence-sequence width.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive experiments improve data use -> ordinary inference can fail after adaptation or stopping -> AIPW scores restore efficient anytime ATE inference -> distributional decisions require the same guarantee for the whole QTE curve

method_exemplars.technique: Lift the adaptive AIPW martingale score, predictable nuisance estimation, propensity truncation, and empirical-Bernstein mixture proof to threshold-indexed potential-outcome CDF scores.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The QTE process is obtained by inverting two counterfactual CDF processes whose efficient scores are functional analogues of the paper's adaptive AIPW score.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its value-uniform betting construction and importance-weighted counterfactual CDF bands, then sharpen them using augmentation and local variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already handles a whole counterfactual distribution under arbitrary data dependence, the immediate precursor to a response-adaptive QTE band.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse its uniform quantile-process linearization and treatment-control covariance accounting after replacing the fixed-sample empirical process by a predictable martingale process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the econometric QTE-process target and uniform-in-quantile inferential structure absent from adaptive ATE work.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax welfare-regret versus whole-QTE-band-width frontier when adaptive assignment probabilities may vanish, including the exploration threshold below which some quantiles cease to be consistently inferable.

source_refs.claim: Uses a vanishing Bernoulli-mixture sequence to trade welfare regret against shrinking anytime-valid ATE confidence sequences for general bandit algorithms.
source_refs.author: Biyonka Liang and Iavor Bojinov
source_refs.venue: arXiv / Harvard Business School Working Paper

source_refs.claim: Characterizes a Pareto trade-off between cumulative bandit regret and statistical power for mean treatment-effect inference.
source_refs.author: David Simchi-Levi and Chonghuan Wang

source_refs.claim: Shows that adaptive importance-weighted whole-CDF bands remain valid but may be trivial, with convergence controlled by an instance-dependent effective-sample condition.
source_refs.author: Paul Mineiro and Steven R. Howard

source_refs.claim: Establishes the optimal LIL rate for whole-quantile confidence sequences under i.i.d. sampling and studies quantile best-arm identification.
source_refs.author: Steven R. Howard and Aaditya Ramdas

open_problems.why_unsolved: Mean-effect welfare-inference trade-offs depend mainly on inverse-propensity moments, whereas QTE precision is quantile-specific: rare tail events and small outcome densities may require substantially more exploration than central quantiles. Existing adaptive CDF bands acknowledge that validity can coexist with trivial width, while existing regret frontiers do not identify which portions of a causal quantile curve remain estimable as exploration decays.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching minimax lower and upper bounds for cumulative welfare regret and quantile-indexed confidence-sequence width, including a necessary-and-sufficient exploration exponent for uniform consistency on a stated quantile interval and an attaining mixed-bandit design.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest motivation arc for protecting participant welfare while preserving optional-stopping-valid causal inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bandits reduce exposure to inferior arms -> vanishing exploration destroys ordinary causal precision -> mixing restores a shrinking ATE confidence sequence -> distributional decisions require the sharp exploration threshold for an entire QTE curve

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its minimax multi-objective formulation and necessary-and-sufficient Pareto condition from scalar power to a quantile-indexed width functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly formalizes the welfare-versus-inference conflict, but the proposed resolution replaces mean power with simultaneous QTE precision.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its importance-weighted CDF supermartingales and effective-sample convergence condition to translate decaying exploration into quantile-specific band widths.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its sometimes-trivial counterfactual CDF bands expose the inferential failure that a frontier theorem must characterize.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the empirical-process LIL lower-rate benchmark and CDF inversion to calibrate the best possible width once effective arm sample sizes are fixed.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the sharp nonadaptive endpoint against which losses from regret-minimizing exploration can be measured.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a realized-quadratic-variation pivot that is simultaneously uniform over monitoring time and quantile index for the whole finite-population QTE curve under known predictable adaptive randomization.

source_refs.excerpt: Position the early-measurable-scale self-normalized martingale step against the closest Hall--Heyde/de la Pena
at most \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\) nonempty averaging sets can occur

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior adaptive-experiment theorem uses a scalar early-measurable random scale, whereas QTE inversion begins with two indicator martingales indexed by every outcome threshold. Scalar self-normalization does not control a random covariance kernel, crossings over an uncountable threshold class, or nonsmooth CDF inversion. Conversely, the prior whole-function band handles finitely many candidate sets at a fixed horizon through a conditional union bound, which cannot deliver the sharp log-log time penalty. The first missing step is therefore a threshold-indexed self-normalized maximal inequality or strong approximation driven by the observed covariance kernel.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A randomization-valid confidence sequence for the full QTE curve with simultaneous time-and-quantile coverage, observable realized-kernel studentization, and a theorem identifying its uniform LIL half-width under explicit allocation and quantile-spacing conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames inferential failure as a same-path consequence of adaptive treatment assignment and builds the remedy around predictable weighting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive experiments concentrate assignments using accrued outcomes -> ordinary fixed-design inference loses calibration -> predictable weighting restores causal inference -> a threshold-indexed pivot is needed for anytime whole-curve QTE inference

method_exemplars.technique: Use self-normalized exponential inequalities and martingale comparison arguments with random quadratic variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The source theorem is built around realized-QV self-normalization; the new object is its function-indexed analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Mix exponential supermartingales and stitch intrinsic-time epochs to prove nonasymptotic time-uniform LIL boundaries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the temporal crossing control that the fixed-horizon empirical-process band lacks.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert sequential CDF confidence sequences into quantile confidence sequences while preserving time-uniform coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The final QTE band arises through joint inversion of the two potential-outcome CDF processes.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an observable anytime whole-curve QTE band that remains uniformly honest across positive-density quantiles, vanishing-density cusps, and atoms while attaining the correct regime-specific LIL width.

source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Iván Fernández-Val, Blaise Melly, and Kaspar Wüthrich
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Provides time- and value-uniform importance-weighted CDF bands but not sharp outcome-scale QTE shrinkage results at atoms.
source_refs.author: Paul Mineiro and Steven R. Howard

source_refs.claim: Its efficient response-adaptive QTE allocation relies on densities, leaving atomic and vanishing-density regimes outside the regular variance calculation.
source_refs.author: Zhonghua Li, Lan Luo, Jingshen Wang, and Long Feng

source_refs.excerpt: supplies neither uniform anti-concentration nor an observable common-multiplier coupling through variance degeneracy
a finite-sample globally calibrated band and a general full-observed-law width obstruction

open_problems.why_unsolved: At atoms or cusps, regular QTE bands lose their uniform inverse-density linearization: an LIL-sized CDF band may map to a nonshrinking or discontinuously shrinking outcome-scale set. Predictable inverse-probability weights further make each arm's effective sample size allocation-dependent. Static discrete-QTE inversion establishes validity but not the sequential shrinkage frontier, while regular adaptive-QTE efficiency relies on densities that do not cover this regime. Prior work also records the failure of observable multiplier coupling through degeneracy and does not establish a local-oracle width ratio, so the first replacement is a sequential CDF coupling with an observable two-sided inverse-modulus certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A single anytime-valid set-valued QTE band with simultaneous time-and-quantile coverage and matching upper and lower width bounds that reduce to the density-based LIL rate at regular quantiles and the appropriate inverse-modulus rate at cusps or atoms.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly motivates why conventional quantile-process inference fails for discrete outcomes and formulates CDF-band inversion as the remedy.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Quantile effects are policy-relevant -> discrete outcomes invalidate regular quantile asymptotics -> simultaneous CDF-band inversion recovers honest QTE sets -> adaptive monitoring requires a sharp mixed-regime LIL-width characterization

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over left- and right-inverse transformations of simultaneous distribution-function bands and Minkowski differencing for quantile effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The set-valued inversion handles atoms without imposing a fictitious positive density, matching the irregular target.

method_exemplars.technique: Supply predictable importance-weighted, time-and-value-uniform CDF bands as the input to irregular quantile inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the adaptive sequential input band while the discrete-QTE paper supplies the nonlinear output transformation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use directional differentiability, characterize ordinary bootstrap failure, and construct a derivative-aware inferential correction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Quantile inversion at atoms or zero density is directionally rather than fully differentiable, the obstruction behind a mixed regular-nonregular limit theorem.

open_problems.open_problem: Give minimal observable support and branch-mass conditions for uniform realized-QV studentization of an adaptive whole-curve QTE process, and prove that a lower bound on conditional outcome variance alone is insufficient.

source_refs.excerpt: the present Var(Y|F_{t-1}) lower bound does not itself certify failure-relevant observable nondegeneracy

open_problems.why_unsolved: For QTE inference the score variance must accumulate for every threshold used in inversion, not merely for the raw outcome. Positive conditional variance may be carried entirely by observations outside a quantile's informative branch, leaving the corresponding armwise indicator score with zero or vanishing quadratic variation. The cited reviewer identifies this gap for a scalar adaptive counterexample through missing support probabilities, branch mass, and failure magnitude; the first proof step for the curve is a uniform threshold-by-threshold decomposition of predictable and realized quadratic variation with explicit allocation positivity and two-sided outcome mass near every target quantile.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem in observable armwise support, allocation, and local CDF-mass terms yielding uniform-in-time QTE studentization, paired with adaptive potential-outcome counterexamples having positive conditional outcome variance but degenerate quantile-score quadratic variation and invalid coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly separates adaptive-design pathology, overlap-like conditions, and a repair based on predictable weights.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome-adaptive assignment creates unstable information -> predictable reweighting can restore scalar effect inference -> validity still depends on information accumulation -> QTE curves require local accumulation at every inversion threshold

method_exemplars.technique: Relate self-normalized concentration and asymptotics to divergence and regularity of realized quadratic variation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The positive theorem must identify when the quantile-score normalizer genuinely accumulates enough information.

method_exemplars.technique: Express quantile uncertainty through sequential counts below candidate thresholds and invert their confidence sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those threshold counts expose why raw outcome variance is not the relevant nondegeneracy condition.

method_exemplars.technique: Use predictable adaptive weights and martingale limit arguments under explicit effective-sample-size conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its information-stability conditions are the scalar template for local arm-by-threshold conditions.

literature_map:
Firpo (2007, Econometrica, 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00738.x) establishes regular semiparametric efficiency for fixed-quantile QTE estimation.
Zhang and Zheng (2020, Quantitative Economics, 10.3982/QE1323) give fixed-horizon uniform-in-quantile QTE limits and bootstrap bands under covariate-adaptive randomization.
Li, Luo, Wang, and Feng (2025, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2024.105857) design response-adaptive experiments attaining a quantile-specific QTE efficiency bound.
Howard and Ramdas (2022, Bernoulli, 10.3150/21-BEJ1388; arXiv:1906.09712) obtain i.i.d. confidence sequences for all quantiles with the optimal LIL rate.
Mineiro and Howard (2023, NeurIPS, 10.52202/075280-0278; arXiv:2302.14248) obtain time- and value-uniform CDF bands under nonstationarity, including importance-weighted counterfactual bands that may be trivial.
Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe, and Sekhon (2021, Annals of Statistics, 10.1214/20-AOS1991) provide mixture-bound and empirical-Bernstein confidence-sequence machinery.
Waudby-Smith, Arbour, Sinha, Kennedy, and Ramdas (2024, Annals of Statistics, 10.1214/24-AOS2408; arXiv:2103.06476) use strong invariance principles for asymptotic time-uniform causal inference.
Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024, AISTATS; arXiv:2311.18274) combine efficient adaptive AIPW estimation with ATE confidence sequences and flag non-ATE estimands as future work.
Ham, Bojinov, Lindon, and Tingley (2022, arXiv:2210.08639) construct design-based confidence sequences for adaptive experiments, centered on mean effects.
Liang and Bojinov (2023, arXiv:2311.05794) use vanishing Bernoulli mixing to expose a welfare-regret versus anytime-ATE-inference trade-off.
Simchi-Levi and Wang (2023, AISTATS, PMLR 206) characterize Pareto-optimal welfare-regret and mean-effect-power trade-offs.
Dai, Gradu, and Harshaw (2023, NeurIPS; arXiv:2305.17187) define Neyman regret and prove a square-root-time design-based ATE guarantee.
Noarov, Fogliato, Bertran, and Roth (2025, ICML; arXiv:2502.17427) sharpen design-based ATE Neyman regret to anytime logarithmic order.
Neopane, Ramdas, and Singh (2025, AISTATS; arXiv:2411.14341) obtain logarithmic superpopulation Neyman regret for ATE allocation.
Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, Melly, and Wüthrich (2020, JASA, 10.1080/01621459.2019.1611581) handle discrete QTE bands by transforming CDF bands; none of the located papers combines irregular inversion, response-adaptive allocation regret, and sharp LIL width.

The solve artifacts for exp_ani_annealed_hac_exactness and exp_boundedcluster_endpoint_orbit_minimax were inspected but did not yield a comparably direct QTE-anytime opportunity.
